# Third independent review: NSSCO Development Studies 6136 (Grades 10–11)

This was a read-only review. I made no edits and ran no scripts, web searches or subagents. I did not take Codex's audit results or repair notes as proof; I checked repaired passages against their actual text.

## Verdict: **FIX CONTENT BEFORE PUBLICATION**

I found nothing critical. The notes are accurate on the points I checked, the 16 numerical examples I re-derived hold up, and the research section correctly keeps the invented demonstration separate from the learner's own enquiry. But several medium-severity problems remain. Four are new, and three are leftovers from earlier repairs: the 4.2 work-status passage, the 7.3-006 rebuild and the new SDG paragraph. They affect how learners pace long answers, one taught fact that isn't in a prompt, and learner-facing wording. The plan itself does not need fixing. This review is not teacher verification and does not authorise publication.

## Findings

| ID | Sev. | Locator | Finding and learner consequence | Repair | Conf. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R3-01 | Medium (analysis) | Part (b) of P01 in 5.1, 6.1, 6.2, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 8.1, 9.1, 9.2 and 9.3 | **The model answers for 4-mark "Explain" parts are one or two clauses long.** Example: 6.2-P01(b) says only "Transport and timetable barriers prevent use of the formal opportunity, so practical arrangements must be assessed; written admission alone cannot establish access." That is about two credit points. The P01 answers in topics 1.1–4.2 are properly developed. Learners will calibrate their answer length to the short versions and lose marks. | Expand each (b) answer to four distinct creditable steps, using the 1.1-P01/2.2-P01 pattern. | 0.85 |
| R3-02 | Medium (coherence) | Final "Apply…/Read the practical connection/Worked enquiry connection" blocks in 5.1–10.1, e.g. BLK-6.1.03-07, 6.2.04-02, 7.3.01-04, 8.1.03-07, 10.1.10-05 | **These notes blocks are card prompts pasted word for word with their answers attached.** Example: "Name and describe stratified sampling for this fictional task: … Stratified sampling: Allocate eight and four…". The rendered notes contain the same text (e.g. `topics/8.1/8.1-politics-and-development.md:111`). Learners read the answer to a card before they try it, so the card stops testing recall. The prose also reads as unfinished. This is the continuing part of R6136-015. | Rewrite these blocks as worked explanations with different numbers or cases from the cards, or drop them where an Applied example already covers the point. | 0.9 |
| R3-03 | Medium (accuracy) | BLK-6136-4.2.05-04 (the N-02 repair) | **The survey population is described in a way that contradicts the data.** The block says "100 people available for and seeking more work", then counts 30 of them as having "their desired hours". People with their desired hours are not seeking more work. Card 4.2-022 correctly says "available for work". This muddies the exact distinction the repair was meant to teach. | Change the block to "100 people available for work". | 0.95 |
| R3-04 | Medium (fact not supplied, Q2) | ITEM-6136-10.1-P02, answers A2(2) and A2(4) | **The answer depends on a fact the prompt doesn't give.** It says usable bags rise "from 80 to 120", which assumes the spoiled bags are counted inside the 100 and 130 output totals. The stem gives the two figures separately. A learner who reads output as usable output would be marked wrong by guidance that relies on an unstated assumption. | Add to the stem "spoiled bags are included in output", or accept both readings. | 0.8 |
| R3-05 | Medium (coherence/curriculum) | ITEM-6136-7.3-006 vs BLK-6136-7.3.02-02 (the N-05 repair) | **The card and the notes describe different scenarios.** On the card, the apprenticeship has "no formal qualification". In the notes, it "offers… preparation for a recognised assessment" and an allowance. The two versions also reach different conclusions. Neither uses the objective's own terms: OBJ-7.3.02-00 asks for advantages and disadvantages of *traditional and modern education systems*, and the card never links apprenticeship to traditional or college to modern. A learner who studied the notes will bring the wrong facts to the card. | Bring the notes block into line with the card, and add one sentence in each mapping the routes to traditional and modern education. | 0.85 |
| R3-06 | Medium (learner-facing provenance) | BLK-6136-1.2.01-R01 | **Internal pipeline wording appears in learner text.** The notes say "The saved 2022 examination figure shows examples including…", which refers learners to an internal exam artefact they do not have. The same SDG list leaves out Quality Education, Gender Equality and Climate Action. These are the answers the 2023 examiner report accepts, and 2022 P2 asked about Goal 13. | Remove the provenance wording and present the goals directly. Name a fuller set of goals, including 4, 5 and 13, with one line on why climate action matters to sustainable development. | 0.9 |
| R3-07 | Medium (tariff/guidance) | ITEM-6136-1.2-006 | **The answer asks for more than the 3 marks allow, and the guidance doesn't credit half of it.** The prompt wants a suggested action, a reason *and* two SDGs. The guidance awards only context and reason, with nothing for the SDGs. The SDG 8 link depends on "if the bags provide decent paid work", which the prompt doesn't state. | Either raise the tariff to 4 and credit the SDGs, or ask for one SDG. Make paid work explicit in the stem. | 0.85 |
| R3-08 | Low–medium (guidance) | ITEM-6136-2.2-003 (the N-06 repair) | **The marking guidance is left over from the old card.** It still says "shorter implementation priorities versus the longer national development direction", but the new prompt compares two HPP pillars. The answer also calls the pillars "shorter-term pillars… to Vision 2030"; the notes never name Vision 2030 in the HPP paragraph. Separately, 2022 P2(a)(v) asks learners to *describe three* HPP pillars [3], and the examiner report says most only listed them. No card practises this. | Rewrite the guidance, and add a 3-mark "describe three pillars" card based on BLK-2.2.02-R01. | 0.9 |
| R3-09 | Low (curriculum) | Topic 1.2 and BLK-2.2.02-03 | **Exam terminology is missing.** No card asks learners to identify the economic, social and environmental pillars of sustainable development (2022 Q1(b)(i), "poorly answered"). The NDP5 notes describe its "goals" but never use the pillar names the exam uses, e.g. "Economic Progression" in the 2022 Fig. 3 stimulus. | Add a 1–2 mark pillars card. Add one sentence giving NDP5's pillar labels next to the goals. | 0.75 |
| R3-10 | Low (tidiness) | BLK-6136-10.1.10-06; guidance for 8.1-025…031 | Learner notes cite internal item IDs ("(ITEM-6136-10.1-P01)"). The 8.1 guidance reuses notes sentences instead of marking criteria. | Remove the IDs, and write the guidance as marking points. | 0.9 |

Results on the six reviewer questions, beyond the table above:
- **Causal validity:** no causal mechanism is inverted. The ones I traced include GNP per person, urban share versus urban count, fixed-cost economies of scale, malaria transmission versus water-borne transmission, the investment inflow versus the goods balance, and the woodland and channel balances.
- **Conditions:** these are generally carried through to the cards (maintenance, demand, buyers, consent).
- **Numbers:** apart from R3-04, the methods and interpretations are sound. This covers percentage change versus percentage points, ‰ versus %, the pie and divided-rectangle specifications, and the systematic interval and start.
- **Package tariffs:** all four sum to 50, split 35 for Section A and 15 for Section B.

## Disposition of earlier findings (checked against the current text)

| ID | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| N-01 | **Resolved (sampled)** | Teaching paragraphs are restored in the blocks I checked: 10.1 random/stratified/systematic definitions, questionnaires and interviews, 7.2 diet, 5.1 groups and colonial influences, 6.1 food stages. I did not count all 66. The pasted-card problem in R3-02 is new and separate. |
| N-02 | **Partially resolved** | The totals are now correctly explained as overlapping. The population wording is still contradictory (R3-03). |
| N-03 | **Open** | The HPP claim now correctly cites 2022 ER Q1(a). The SDG, 2016 EU–SADC EPA, South Africa/India and similar claims cite only a generic "syllabus-and-local-assessment-corpus" derivation. The 2016 EPA cannot be confirmed from local sources. All claims remain unverified. |
| N-04 | **Resolved** | 8.1-025…031 and 9.2-011…016 now have specific, natural prompts. Minor guidance issue in R3-10. |
| N-05 | **Partially resolved** | The card is reframed and has a judgement. It still diverges from the notes and doesn't map to the objective (R3-05). |
| N-06 | **Partially resolved** | 2.2-004 now uses the taught NDP5 goals. 2.2-003 has stale guidance, and the 3-pillar demand is untested (R3-08). |
| N-07 | **Resolved** | The guidance headers of all four packages no longer refer to a fictional model. |
| N-08 | **Not checked** | I did not open slot-demand-specs.json. This file is not learner-facing. |
| R6136-004 | **Partially resolved** | The SDG examples, the three pillars and an SDG card were added. Open issues: provenance wording, missing goals, tariff and guidance (R3-06, R3-07, R3-09). |
| R6136-015 | **Open** | Repeated scenarios remain: blocked road or bridge (1.1-026, 4.2-019, 5.1-P01/056, 9.1-025, 9.3-P01/002), 3.1 missing-input cases ×5, and 30→10 losses. Notes now duplicate card prose (R3-02). |

## Two learner tests (from the notes alone)

**Test 1 — "Name and describe random, stratified and systematic sampling" [6]**
- From BLK-10.1.10-02/03/04 a learner would write:
  - **Random:** every member of the defined population has an equal chance of selection. Number a complete list and draw distinct numbers fairly; picking whoever is nearest doesn't count.
  - **Stratified:** divide the population into relevant groups, allocate places in proportion to each group's size (40/20 → 8/4), then select randomly within each group.
  - **Systematic:** take every k-th entry from an ordered list after a fair start (60/12 → interval 5, start 3: 3, 8, 13…). A repeating pattern in the list can cause bias.
- **Result: full marks.** The notes also separate sample from sampling method (10.1-059), which the corpus analysis identifies as a common exam confusion.

**Test 2 — "Evaluate farmers' cooperatives and resettlement as rural development strategies in Southern Africa, including implementation problems" [high tariff]**
- From BLK-5.1.04-03/04/R01/R02 a learner can give several distinct benefits of cooperatives: bulk purchasing, shared transport, storage, bargaining, credit links and advice.
- Cooperative problems: fair rules, trustworthy records, conflicting member interests.
- Resettlement benefit: wider land access in Namibian land reform. Resettlement problems: water, services, skills, buyers, consent, social disruption (5.1-027).
- A conditional judgement is modelled.
- **Result: likely top band.** The only weakness is that the Namibian detail is thin and unsourced (N-03).

**Additional probe:** 2022-style "Explain why Goal 13 is important for sustainable development" [3] **would fail**, because the notes contain no climate-action content (R3-06).

## Coverage

- **All 18 topics:** I read every lesson block and every item in the supplied packet — 505 cards and 38 activities, including all four research packages with their stimuli, answers, tariffs and Section B scaffolds.
- **Repaired cards** read closely: 1.2-006, 2.2-003/004/P01, 4.2-022, 7.3-006, 8.1-025…031, 9.2-011…018, and the 10.1 packages.
- **At least 20 cards per topic** were checked across subtypes; for 2.1, 2.2, 1.2 and 9.3 that meant all of them.
- **Sources checked by search:** 2022 P2 and ER, 2023 ER and 2020 P1/P2 SDG/HPP extracts; syllabus-facts; four registry objectives; claim ledgers for 1.2, 2.2, 5.1 and 9.3; the section 6 rows of the second review and the full second repair report.

## Limitations

- **Not read:** AGENTS.md, TEAM-PLAYBOOK, both profiles, PLAN, HANDOVER (one line only), work orders' excluded sections, the contract and the slot specs. The plan- and contract-level scope check is therefore **partial**; the content review is complete.
- **Codex audit figures** (749 unverified claims, 0 deterministic failures, 16 numerical checks, 0 copied-wording matches) come from Codex's runs. I did not repeat them. C35/C41/C43 are not_run and have not passed.
- **No external verification:** dated facts were checked only against local sources and my own knowledge — HPP 2016/Geingob, NDP5 2017/18–2021/22, Singapore 1987, China 2015, SACU membership. The 2016 EPA rests on my own knowledge only, as no local source covers it.
- **Not checked:** rendered charts and maps.
- **No specialist subject approval.**
